page.layout: One column of running text, set in the middle of the page. Page number "152" at top left, running head "NOTÆ." at top right. No marginal notes. Catchword "ejus" at the foot, right.

main_text.p: notus Arabismus iste. من دخل ظفار حمير Qui Dhafarum ingreditur, (urbs ea, Regum Hamyarensium sedes) Hamyarismum addiscat, quae verbum in proverbium abierunt, quo monetur quis eorum quibus cohabitat, moribus|se accommodare. Hinc autem (uti diximus) patet Hamyarensium Dialectum ad Hebraicam vel Syriacam, sive Chaldaicam in quibusdam, propius accedere, (ut & ipsos ad Judaismum inclinasse in superioribus vidimus) ذن[?] enim Hamyarin-fibus[?] idem sonat ac Hebraeis ישב[?] Syris & Chaldaeis יתב[?] a quo in Imperativo ישב[?] Sedere. at communi Arabum dialecto contrariam habet notionem, Saltandi sc. vel Subsiliendi. Praeterea in Regis responso quod عربيت[?] litera claudatur quod Arabes per ꝫ[?] efferre solent, Syrismum etiam sapere videtur. Per linguam autem istam cujus peritiae operam dedisse Arabes asserit Author noster, Dialectum istam Koraifhitarum defaecatam & politam praecipuè intelligi credo, quae quâ ratione caeteris elegantior evaserit describit Jalaloddinus in lib. Mezh. c. 9. scil. quòd dum Templi Meccani aedituï essent & Arabia centrum incolerent non solùm à caeteris Gentibus (quarum vicinia & commercio aliarum Tribuum sermo vitii aliquid contraxerat) remotiores essent, sed & confluentibus undequaque Meccam Arabibus tum religionis ergò, tum ut lites suas ad ipsos componendas deferrent, ex eorum sermone & carminibus puriores ac elegantiores quascunque sive dictiones, sive loquendi formulas & phrases, selectas, suas facerent, adeò ut in ipsorum Dialectum omnes universi quaquâ patet Arabismi elegantiae confluxerint. Linguae autem suae in Encomium multa congerunt, atque inter caetera, immensa ejus[catchword]

page.notes: Arabic and Hebrew words are copied from the scan and are doubtful where marked [?]: the Arabic after "enim", the Hebrew forms ישב and יתב, and the Arabic word before "litera". The Hebrew and Arabic at the start of the first line is read with reasonable confidence. The character after "per" is unclear. "Hamyarin-fibus" at the line end is doubtful. The word "ejus" appears at the foot as a catchword and is also the last word of the text, so it is printed once in the paragraph and once in the catchword. Long s is written as s throughout.
